entries.note: Zeller 2008 abstract (PMID 18776916) re-read; quote verbatim. Rinat murine antibodies are fremanezumab's lineage; fremanezumab sc opener, untested not_measured holds.

entries.rule: Retrodiction: an engagement model first public after a patient result for the same target (member or not) is retro, never same
entries.note: Vermeersch 2015 (PMID 26116630, epub 2015-06-26) quote verbatim; galcanezumab SC in HVs right. Model first public after Bigal 2014 (2014-03-24) and Dodick 2014 (2014-08-10) same-target results: retrodiction true, retro not same.
entries.adjudication_note: Retrodiction rule: engagement is a target claim; Vermeersch 2015 (epub 2015-06) was first public after same-target anti-CGRP patient results (Dodick 2014 Phase 2s), so the reproduced human CIDBF is retro, never same.

entries.note: Zeller 2008 abstract quote verbatim; duration of blockade only, no human exposure target. Fremanezumab sc untested no_prediction holds.

Vermeersch 2015 quote verbatim; galcanezumab's own Phase 2 (Dodick 2014, SC 150 mg q2w, epub 2014-08-10) public first, so retro/retrodiction true is right. Galcanezumab sc dose track has no opener; margin from tox NOAEL is a rule question.
Zeller 2008 abstract quote verbatim; explicit migraine-prevention prediction opens the fremanezumab sc track (product_in_model false).

Bigal 2015 Lancet Neurol (PMID 26432182, epub 2015-09-30) quote verbatim; primary migraine-days endpoint met at SC 225/675 mg. NCT02025556 first posted 2014-01-01 (CT.gov). Same 2015 on fremanezumab sc holds.
Kopruszinski abstract quote verbatim (PMID 27206958, epub 2016-05-19, TEV-48125), after Bigal 2015: retro on fremanezumab sc holds.
Melo-Carrillo 2017 (PMID 28642283, epub 2017-06-22) quote verbatim; fremanezumab in rats after Phase 2b: retro on fremanezumab sc holds.
Zeller 2008 quote verbatim; null CV prediction opens the fremanezumab sc safety track.

entries.rule: Track = model_id x drug x route; route is the route the drug was given by in the patients compared
entries.note: Bigal 2014 (PMID 24662322, epub 2014-03-24) quote verbatim, but LBR-101 was IV ('telemetry ... after infusion completion'), so route iv, a fremanezumab iv track needing its own opener; status same holds there.
entries.adjudication_note: Status rule: no BP/HR/ECG change in dosed humans matches the rat null prediction. Track rule: LBR-101 was infused, so route is iv, a fremanezumab iv track that needs its own untested opener (rule 6).

entries.note: 761063 SumR (bundle text) quote verbatim; galcanezumab Phase 3 SC pool, so galcanezumab sc same 2018 holds. Track has no opener before 2018.

de Vries Lentsch 2022 (PMID 36195452, epub 2022-10-04) fremanezumab-arm quote verbatim; SC fremanezumab migraine cohort; contra 2022 under rule 6 holds (uncontrolled pre-post cohort, medium confidence).
Ohlsson 2018 (PMID 30109438) quote verbatim; fremanezumab is the product in the rings, sc is its patient route. No dosed-human arterial readout exists; untested not_measured holds.
Ohlsson 2018 aim sentence verbatim; opener at first use on fremanezumab sc holds.
Ohlsson 2018 conclusion quote verbatim; run after HALO CM/EM, so retro on fremanezumab sc holds.
Mason 2017 (PMID 28053042) quote verbatim; opener of the eptinezumab iv track at first antibody use (ALD405 sibling, product_in_model false) holds.
Mason 2017 quote verbatim; post-dates Dodick 2014b ALD403 IV Phase 2 (2014-10-05): retro on eptinezumab iv holds.
Christensen 2019 (PMID 31288556, epub 2019-07-09) quote verbatim; eptinezumab iv opener 2019 holds.
Christensen 2019 quote verbatim; after PROMISE-1/2, retro on eptinezumab iv holds.

NCT04464707 (fremanezumab SC, 6-17 y CM) results first posted 2025-12-19 per CT.gov; AAN 2026 abstract quote verbatim; DOI resolves (Neurology suppl). Drug, route, year 2025 right; pediatric-miss rule question 1 still open.
Vermeersch 2015 abstract quote verbatim; galcanezumab in NHP CIDBF before FIH (2011 proxy). Galcanezumab sc opener holds; untested_reason null fine (not track's latest).
Dodick 2014 (PMID 25127173, epub 2014-08-10) quote verbatim; primary endpoint met, SC 150 mg q2w; NCT01625988. Prospective Zeller 2008 pairing: same 2014 on galcanezumab sc holds.
Zeller 2008 quote verbatim; no ALD403 run in this system, class prediction from sibling antibody; eptinezumab iv opener 2008 holds.

Dodick 2014b (PMID 25297013, epub 2014-10-05) quote verbatim; single 1000 mg IV, primary efficacy endpoint wk 5-8 met one-sided (primary objective safety, said in note). Same 2014 on eptinezumab iv holds.
761063s010 label (Revised 3/2025) fetched; section 5.3 quote verbatim. No earlier galcanezumab-specific BP signal; contra 2025 on galcanezumab sc holds.

entries.rule: Rule 2: a regulator document (FDA review or label) is source_tier 2
entries.note: 761119 SumR (bundle text) quote verbatim (rat 4-wk, monkey 6-mo IV tox, no adverse effects). Untested 2013 proxy opener holds, but source_tier should be 2 (FDA summary review), not 1.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 2: FDA summary review is source_tier 2, not 1; status untested stands as the 2013 proxy opener of the eptinezumab iv track (rule 6). Not the track's latest entry, so no untested_reason.

entries.note: Dodick 2014b abstract quote verbatim (no vital-sign differences, 1000 mg IV); same 2014 on eptinezumab iv holds.
761119s009s012 label (Revised 3/2025) fetched; section 5.3 quote verbatim. No earlier eptinezumab-specific BP signal; contra 2025 on eptinezumab iv holds.

missing: Fremanezumab pediatric chronic migraine Phase 3 NCT04464707 (6-17 y): primary endpoint NOT met, LS mean difference -0.1 MMD (95% CI -1.48 to 1.22), p=0.8484, placebo -3.7 vs fremanezumab -3.8; CT.gov results posted 2025-12-19 (tier 3); AAN 2026 abstract Hershey et al. (index.mirasmart.com/AAN2026/PDFfiles/AAN2026-001129.html) states 'no significant difference was observed between treatment groups in the CM study (-3.8 vs -3.7; p=0.8484)'. A member-drug primary-endpoint miss in the context disease with no entry on the efficacy track; companion EM study NCT04458857 was positive (-2.5 vs -1.4, p=0.0210; label s031 adds pediatric EM). Whether it scores contra is rule question 1.

Human ex-vivo artery model: Ohlsson et al. 2018, 'Fremanezumab blocks CGRP induced dilatation in human cerebral, middle meningeal and abdominal arteries', J Headache Pain, doi 10.1186/s10194-018-0905-8 (PMID 30109438, 2018-08-14): model_kind ex_vivo, product_in_model true, retrodiction after Phase 3; no track in the draft.

Mouse CGRP-evoked light-aversion / spontaneous-pain models blocked by ALD405 (eptinezumab's murine sibling, Alder): Mason et al. 2017 J Neurosci doi 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2967-16.2016 (PMID 28053042) and Rea et al. 2018 Pain doi 10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001337 (PMID 29994995): retrodiction track, product_in_model false; no track in the draft.

Rodent GTN / migraine-like pain models with ALD405 and olcegepant: Christensen et al. 2019 Cephalalgia doi 10.1177/0333102419861726 (PMID 31288556, 2019-07-09): retrodiction, product_in_model false; no track in the draft.

Rat post-concussion headache model (Bree & Levy, Cephalalgia, doi 10.1177/0333102416681571, epub 2016-12-07) is filed in the 761089 PharmR as a paradigm distinct from the MOH model; the draft folds it into rat-headache-behaviour without an entry or source of its own. Acceptable as one track, but the PharmR citation should be recorded.

For the record, not scoring: CHALLENGE-MIG NCT05127486 (galcanezumab vs rimegepant, Lilly 2024 release) missed superiority on >=50% responder, an active-comparator endpoint no model predicted; galcanezumab chronic cluster headache and fremanezumab ENFORCE cluster headache (futility, 2018-2019) are another disease (MONDO cluster headache), outside this context.
rule_questions: Pediatric-population miss: fremanezumab failed its primary endpoint in pediatric chronic migraine (NCT04464707, 2025) after matching in adults. Under 'patients of the context's disease only' and 'one drug's contra still beats another drug's same', does a pediatric placebo-controlled miss flip an Unselected (adult-derived) efficacy track to contra, or is age a population split the context does not cover?

Efficacy cell on a PD-only system: when the only prospective preclinical system is a target-engagement model (evoked vasodilation) whose authors nonetheless made an explicit efficacy prediction (Zeller 2008), does efficacy score same on that track, or is the cell the empty list because no disease model was relied on? The draft's context note says 'not on a disease model' yet populates the cell.

readout_tier for in-vivo blockade of an evoked stimulus (capsaicin-induced dermal blood flow): the rule lists ex-vivo blockade of a stimulus as direct; in-vivo physiology (blood flow) could be downstream. Undecided.
magnitude for a predicted-null harm that then appeared: 'opposite' is defined for a predicted harm that never appeared; the reverse case (null predicted, hypertension reported) has no stated value.

Dating a class-wide pharmacovigilance harm: a tier-1 prospective cohort pooling a sibling-class drug (erenumab) with a member (fremanezumab) showed BP rising in 2022; does a pooled cohort where the member is the minority arm set the member's comparison date, or only the member-specific label (2025)?

margin_stated on a PD-model track: the tolerability margin comes from the FDA-filed monkey tox NOAEL (a separate study on the same species), not from the CIDBF PK/PD model that is the track's model_id. Does a tox NOAEL count as 'the model stated the margin' for decision 16?

Christensen 2019 runs two paradigms (mouse GTN-provoked allodynia; selectively bred rat spontaneous trigeminal allodynia) with one result under one model_id rodent-gtn-sta-pain. Decision 8 tracks each system; does one paper/one result justify one track, or should it be split?

Engagement retrodiction on a same-paper PK/PD model: Vermeersch 2015 ran the NHP CIDBF model before first-in-human (2011) but first published it in 2015, after galcanezumab and LBR-101 patient results on the same target. Does an earlier efficacy result count as 'a patient result' for the engagement question, making it retro, or only an earlier human readout of the same PD marker?
